The idea that you don’t truly know something until you can teach it is often attributed to physicist Richard Feynman. comments.author: @MikkoRantalainen
comments.text:
Since AGI is about achieving or beating average human performance when it comes to intelligence, I think AGI should be defined as "at least 50% of randomly picked humans consider the candidate AGI system smarter than themselves". I think it's important to ask if the AI is smarter than the responder instead of asking if they feel condidate AI system is smarter than estimated average human intelligence. And to make it statistically significant, you probably have to interview at least 1500 people.

For example, xAI or OpenAI could check if people consider their AI a real AGI simply by asking anybody with longer than e.g. 50 chat history for an opinion about the AI performance level. I would definitely answer that the AI is still too dumb. But I still use AI systems because even modern AI is still a nice tool or have.

ASI is much simpler to define. It's just an AI system that can do any intelligence related task better than any human being. Anyone thinking they can beat the AI can easily demonstrate their abilities by doing at least a single thing that AI cannot do.
